sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Assembly of Bionic Companion Robotic Animals with Speech Synthesizers

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — United States-derived common-law statutory framework anchored on the Constitution of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, with English common-law heritage and a substantive overlay of Marshallese customary law; corporate law is modeled closely on the Delaware General Corporation Law.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Amended Compact of Free Association between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (2003) — reciprocal economic, investment, trade, and assistance framework

Tax Information Exchange Agreement (TIEA) between the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the United States of America (signed 5 May 2011, in force) — active exchange-of-information instrument in the absence of a double taxation agreement
South Pacific Regional Trade and Economic Cooperation Agreement (SPARTECA, 1980) — preferential non-reciprocal trade arrangement with Australia and New Zealand applicable to the Marshall Islands

Samoa Agreement (2023) between the European Union and the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States — successor to the Cotonou Agreement, applicable to the Marshall Islands as a Pacific ACP State

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary instruments: (1) Business Corporations Act 1990 (RMI), as amended, codified at Title 32 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code (MIRC) — governing incorporation, corporate name, registered office, registered agent, record-keeping, and the non-resident tax-exempt corporate regime; (2) Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2018 (RMI), as amended — establishing the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU), customer due diligence (CDD), beneficial-ownership identification, record-keeping, and suspicious-transaction reporting obligations; (3) the FIU's regulatory guidance and supervision manual implementing the FATF Recommendations; and (4) applicable administrative regulations of the Office of the Registrar of Corporations. The beneficial-ownership register is maintained privately by the licensed registered agent in the Marshall Islands; no public UBO register exists, and the record is not filed with the corporate registry but is accessible to the FIU and designated supervisory authorities on lawful demand.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal — Beneficial-ownership data is collected by the licensed registered agent, held in the agent's internal confidential file, and disclosed only to the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit, the Registrar of Corporations, or other competent authorities pursuant to lawful request; no public beneficial-ownership register exists.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of current government-issued photo passport of each individual director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority or public notary in the UBO's country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) where the issuing country is a Contracting Party; otherwise consular legalization through the Marshall Islands consular post or chain legalization via the competent foreign ministry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Beneficial Ownership and Source of Wealth Statutory Declaration of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary in the country of origin of the declaring UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where applicable; otherwise consular legalization at the Marshall Islands consular post with chain authentication

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the licensed Marshall Islands registered agent as attorney-in-fact and agent for service of process
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Subscribers and/or future directors of the business corporation, notarized in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where applicable; otherwise consular legalization in accordance with the law of the country of execution and RMI acceptance practice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of Certificate of Good Standing or certificate of corporate existence and incumbency of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country corporate registry (e.g., Secretary of State, Companies House, or equivalent competent authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where applicable; otherwise consular legalization, plus certified English translation where the original is not in English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified English translation of any document or corporate record issued in a language other than English
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator, with the translator's certification itself notarized in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the notarized translator certification, or consular legalization where the Hague Apostille Convention does not apply

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, registered-agent principals, UBOs, and authorized signatories against: (i) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list (including ISIL/Al-Qaida, Taliban, and DPRK designations); (ii) the US OFAC SDN and non-SDN consolidated sanctions lists; (iii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (iv) domestic RMI FIU notices, advisories, and designations; and (v) commercial Politically Exposed Person (PEP) databases. Screening is conducted at on-boarding, on any trigger event, and on a periodic risk-based basis in accordance with FATF Recommendations 10-12, 22, 24, and 25 as implemented by the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2018. Enhanced due diligence, senior-management sign-off, and source-of-funds/source-of-wealth verification are mandatory for PEPs, natural persons from higher-risk jurisdictions, or atypical transactional structures.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Office of the Registrar of Corporations — Republic of the Marshall Islands Corporate Registry, Majuro; statutory name-search, reservation, and incorporation filings are effected exclusively through licensed Registered Agents approved by the Registrar (there is no direct public self-service online portal for name reservations or incorporations).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the official language of the corporate register. A corporate name must be composed of Latin script characters (A–Z), Arabic numerals (0–9), and permissible punctuation/spacing; if a proposed name is rendered in a non-Latin script, a Latin-character transliteration must be submitted, and the English transliteration governs registerability and distinguishability. The name must end with a corporate identifier such as 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', 'Company', an abbreviation thereof ('Corp.', 'Inc.', 'Ltd.', 'Co.'), or a word of similar import in another language rendered in Latin characters.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banker / Banking — prior consent of the RMI Banking Commissioner required
Trust / Trust Company / Trustee — prior licensing or consent of the relevant RMI financial regulator required
Insurance / Assurance / Reinsurance — prior licensing or consent of the RMI Insurance Commissioner required
Credit Union — prior regulatory authorization required
Co-operative / Cooperative — prior regulatory authorization required
Government / Ministry / Department / Agency — implies RMI or foreign government patronage; prior ministerial written consent required
Municipal / State / Federal / National — implies governmental or supranational status; prior written consent of the competent authority required
Consulate / Embassy / High Commission — implies diplomatic status; prohibited absent the foreign mission's formal written consent
University / College / Institute of Higher Education — prior authorization of the RMI Ministry of Education required
Chamber of Commerce / Board of Trade — prior written consent of the representative body required
Red Cross / Red Crescent — protected international emblems; prior institutional consent required
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal of a proposed name: (1) counsel or the licensed registered agent shall request the Registrar's written reasons for rejection in writing; (2) if the defect is curable (e.g., failing the distinguishability test or containing a sensitive token), file an amended name-reservation application with the required consent letters from the relevant competent authority, ministerial body, or protected-holder institution, and pay the applicable re-filing fee; (3) if the Registrar maintains the refusal, file a formal administrative appeal and request for reconsideration within 15 business days of the dated refusal, supported by written legal argument under the Business Corporations Act 1990 and applicable registry regulations; (4) if the administrative appeal is denied, lodge a petition for judicial review in the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands within 30 days of the denial; and (5) in parallel, reserve one alternative compliant name immediately to preserve transaction timing, noting that a name reservation may be renewed for successive 30-day periods upon payment of the renewal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible and industry-standard for a non-resident Business Corporation with an e-commerce robotic-hardware sales model. No physical premises, local employees, or native business substance in the Marshall Islands is required. The statutory registered office is supplied by the licensed registered agent as a genuine street address in Majuro, which is used for service of process and official correspondence; a bare post-office box is not sufficient to satisfy the Business Corporations Act 1990. This structure preserves the non-resident tax-exempt classification of the entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately 5% annualized probability for this entity class. Unannounced physical on-site inspections by the Registrar of Corporations or the Financial Intelligence Unit are directed primarily at licensed registered agents and local record-keepers, not at the premises of a non-resident company (which typically has no physical presence in the RMI). However, the registered agent's office remains subject to inspection without prior notice, including verification of the UBO file, CDD records, and corporate minute books.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search, name clearance, and name-reservation request (one primary name plus one alternative re-run)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (US$75–US$150 per name-search package); no separate statutory tariff for internal registry search

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Hague Apostille / consular legalization bundle for three origin documents (UBO passport copy, UBO statutory declaration, power of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and apostille/legalization competent authority in the country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document market benchmark of US$60–US$90 per document; consular legalization fees, where applicable, are additional

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial-owner identification, PEP screening, OFAC/UN/EU/domestic sanctions-list screening, and CDD/KYC file preparation by the licensed registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Registered Agent / AML compliance officer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; statutory duty imposed by the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2018

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act, Title 39, Sections 101 (incorporators), 102 (articles of incorporation), 110 (registered office and agent), 121 (directors), and 122 (officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar, Marshall Islands Business Registry, Ministry of Finance, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form BCA-101) together with Certificate of Name Reservation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required; no escrow or bank deposit mandate applies under the Business Corporations Act. Shares may be issued with or without par value as provided in the Articles of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription agreement in the Articles of Incorporation is ratified and subscribers are issued the initially authorized shares for their capital subscriptions. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office and registered agent named in the Articles are adopted as the principal statutory office and process agent. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the President, Secretary, and Treasurer are appointed to serve until the next annual meeting. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the President and Secretary, acting together, are authorized to open bank accounts, apply for licenses, and execute operation start-up instruments; and all prior actions of incorporators are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar, Marshall Islands Business Registry, Majuro.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written name reservation request through the Registry counters or by registered mail with a corporate name containing an appropriate suffix such as 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', or 'Company'. The Registrar will perform a search against active and dissolved corporate registers and reserve the name for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Identity document of the incorporator or director
Power of attorney if filed through a registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused for confusing similarity, the applicant may file an amended name reservation request within seven days or appeal the refusal to the Registrar under Section 103 of the Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation stating the corporate name, authorized share capital, registered office address, registered agent name, directors, and permitted business purpose. Execute the document before a notary public or other officer authorized to administer oaths, with each incorporator signing the original.
required_dossiers: Signed and notarized Articles of Incorporation (original)
Consent to act as director for each initial director
Identity and good standing certificate for any corporate incorporator, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar determines the execution is defective, the incorporator may correct and re-execute the Articles within 14 days of the Notice of Deficiency without re-payment of the full fee if the original filing was valid in substance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar, Marshall Islands Business Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the executed Articles of Incorporation and name reservation certificate to the Registry filing window together with the prescribed filing fee. Payment may be made by bank draft, wire transfer to the Marshall Islands Treasury account, or cashier's check. The Registrar will issue a Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Completed Certificate of Incumbency cover sheet
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried, the applicant will receive a Notice of Correction specifying the defect; the applicant has 21 days from the notice date to submit a curative filing, after which the application may be deemed abandoned and refunds are handled under Treasury rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Registered Agent Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Registered Agent licensee approved by the Office of the Registrar.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a Notice of Registered Office and Registered Agent (Form BCA-110) with the Registry. The registered office must be a physical street address in Majuro, and the agent must be an individual resident or licensed corporate agent appointed to receive service of process on behalf of the corporation.
required_dossiers: Legal opinion or certificate from counsel confirming the designated office is in the Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent declines consent or the office address is found defective, the corporation must file a replacement notice and appoint a substitute agent within 30 days; failure results in automatic appointment of a registered agent by the Registrar under Section 110(d).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial Board of Directors as named in the Articles of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting, or execute unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting, to adopt this first board resolution. The board shall approve share issuance, adopt bylaws, ratify the registered office and agent, and appoint officers. Corporate bank account resolutions and licensing authorization will be recorded in the minutes.
required_dossiers: Unanimous written consent or minutes of organizational meeting
Board resolution approving issuance of shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer or director appointment is invalidated for lack of statutory consent, the board may cure the defect by holding a special meeting and ratifying the appointment with a new written consent; any shares issued in the interim remain valid for good-faith purchasers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Business Licensing Office, Revenue and Taxation Division, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands; Investment approval coordinated with the Marshall Islands Development Authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Manufacturing Business License (Class B) and Foreign Investment Business License (FIBL) for non-resident owned entities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration - Category B (light assembly operation; no full environmental impact assessment required if the facility uses only soldering, low-noise assembly, and dry processes; an Environmental Management Plan must be submitted).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Process wastewater must meet EPA effluent guidelines; zero discharge of untreated process water into lagoon or groundwater is permitted. VOC emissions from soldering and adhesives must remain below 1 ton per year and comply with EPA air quality standards. Lithium-ion battery packaging, electronic scrap, and solder waste must be handled under the EPA Solid Waste Management Regulations; any transboundary movement of e-waste requires prior informed consent under the Basel Convention.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the Majuro Fire and Disaster Prevention Office, structural load inspection certification from the Public Works Inspectorate, and occupational health clearance from the Labor Division covering electrical safety, machine guard compliance, and battery-handling protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) — Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Commerce and Investment; corporate registry portal: https://register.mhr.gov.mh. Fiscal administration is divided between the Ministry of Finance's Revenue and Customs Division (Majuro) for customs duties and the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration (MISSA) for employer payroll contributions. RMI has no national income-tax authority because no corporate or personal income tax is imposed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: RMI does not issue tax identification numbers (TINs), VAT IDs, or income-tax registration numbers. A foreign entity obtains statutory existence by filing Articles of Incorporation with the Registrar of Corporations under MIRC Title 51 (Business Corporations Act) through a licensed RMI registered agent, paying the statutory incorporation filing fee (approximately USD 150), and filing Semi-Annual Reports every six months with the semi-annual license fee (USD 200 per half-year for a non-resident corporation, i.e., USD 400 per annum). No RMI business license or foreign-investment license is required if the non-resident corporation does not maintain an office or operate commercially inside RMI. If the entity imports goods, it must appoint a licensed customs broker in Majuro to obtain an importer registration and post a USD customs bond. If the entity employs RMI-resident staff, it must register as an employer with MISSA using an employer registration number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — an RMI Business Corporation (Non-Resident) is extraterritorially exempt from all national taxation: zero corporate income tax, zero capital gains tax, zero branch profits tax, zero withholding tax on dividends/interest/royalties, zero estate/gift tax, and zero stamp duty. Its passive and active foreign-source income is outside RMI fiscal jurisdiction; the only recurring fiscal costs are the flat semi-annual corporate registry license fees and, if applicable, MISSA contributions for locally hired staff.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under MIRC Title 51, the entity may elect non-resident status (default, tax-neutral) or file a Statement electing resident status, which subjects it solely to the RMI semi-annual license fee schedule; neither status creates income-tax liability. Under MIRC Title 52, the entity may elect to operate as an International Business Corporation (IBC) for enhanced privacy. No check-the-box election exists, and hybrid mismatch, CFC, and BEPS/ATAD rules are inapplicable because RMI levies no corporate income tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No_VAT_GST_Sales_Use_Tax — RMI's only national indirect tax is the customs import duty regime under the Customs Tariff Act (MIRC Title 58), supplemented by specific excise rates on alcohol, tobacco, and fuel; typical ad valorem duty rates range from 3% to 6% on most goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A — RMI imposes no VAT, GST, or sales-and-use tax and therefore has no economic-turnover registration threshold. Customs registration is triggered by the first act of importing goods into RMI, with no minimum value threshold; the importer must use a licensed customs broker and may be required to post a USD bond. Local statutory currency is the United States Dollar (USD).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandate. RMI has no electronic-invoicing obligation, no real-time fiscal clearance regime, no tax-authority API integration, no digital stamping/QR-code clearance, and no continuous transaction controls. Paper or PDF commercial invoices satisfy any commercial record-keeping requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable in the VAT sense: because RMI does not levy VAT, GST, or sales tax on domestic supplies, there is no export zero-rating certificate, input-credit, or VAT-refund mechanism to claim. For RMI customs purposes, goods physically exported from RMI are free of duty and exit the customs territory; robotic AI pet toys manufactured abroad and shipped directly to foreign buyers without entering RMI fall entirely outside the RMI fiscal base, consistent with the non-resident tax-exempt classification. RMI applies no exchange controls; USD is legal tender and inward remittance verification is a banking-commercial convention rather than a statutory obligation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Entry) — mandatory under MIRC Title 58 for any goods physically departing RMI
Bill of Lading (original) or Air Waybill — carrier-issued proof of the export movement
Inward Remittance Certificate — bank-issued proof of USD receipt, required where an export-duty drawback claim or counterparty FX verification is pursued
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: RMI Customs may conduct post-clearance audits of export entries for up to 5 years. False, incomplete, or fraudulent export declarations trigger seizure and forfeiture of the goods, monetary penalties commonly ranging from 100% to 300% of the duty evaded (or a statutory fine up to USD 50,000), and criminal prosecution carrying imprisonment up to 5 years under MIRC Title 58. Because no input VAT is claimable, no export-VAT clawback can arise. Abuse of the non-resident status (e.g., maintaining a local office or conducting RMI-source commercial activity) permits the Registrar to re-assess the resident fee schedule retrospectively, with a 10% late-payment surcharge and deregistration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: None in operation. The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) has no central bank and no foreign exchange administration. The US dollar is the sole legal tender by operation of Article II, Section 212 of the Compact of Free Association (Public Law 108-188), with monetary stability effectively provided by the US Federal Reserve System. Licensing and prudential supervision of deposit-taking institutions rest with the Banking Commissioner (Banking Commission) under the Banking Act 1991, as amended; AML/CFT oversight is exercised by the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2012.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full de jure and de facto convertibility for both current and capital account transactions. Because the RMI issues no domestic currency and imposes no exchange-control statute, there are no approvals, no quantitative limits, no withholding taxes, and no impediments to repatriation of equity, dividends, branch profits, management fees, loan repayments, or liquidation proceeds. All settlements are effected in freely transferable USD via US correspondent clearing; therefore, effective regulatory constraints arise from US OFAC sanctions screening and counterparty bank AML/KYC policies rather than from any RMI FX control. The RMI's tax-exempt regime for non-resident Business Corporations further removes any tax-clearance hurdle to profit remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. The RMI imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender or repatriation obligation on export receipts in USD or any other currency. Export proceeds may be held, converted, or disbursed freely at the exporter's discretion, subject only to general recordkeeping, currency-transaction threshold reporting, and suspicious-transaction reporting obligations under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2012.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Marshall Islands (BMI) — Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands (state-influenced commercial bank, the largest and most established domestic bank)
Bank of Guam, Marshall Islands Branch — Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands (US-regulated foreign bank branch)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD) with access to Bank of Guam's Guam and US clearing networks

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Marshall Islands Development Bank (MIDB) — Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands (statutory development-finance institution)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Not applicable to treasury operations; MIDB does not offer commercial deposit, escrow, or transactional banking services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability rating: MEDIUM-HIGH as an operational disbursement utility, but LOW as a substitute for a licensed RMI bank account and VOID as a licensed RMI entity, because the RMI has no electronic-money institution (EMI) licensing category under the Banking Act 1991 and deposit-taking is reserved to licensed banks. Practical structure: because Stripe does not support the Marshall Islands as a direct merchant jurisdiction, the RMI Business Corporation (BC) should establish a US-incorporated subsidiary (e.g., a Delaware LLC) to serve as merchant of record for Stripe and credit-card acquiring, with daily USD sweeps (ACH/MT103) from the subsidiary to the RMI BC's BMI account; the same US vehicle, or an approved fintech such as Mercury (partnered with Evolve Bank & Trust) or Airwallex, may execute small outbound supplier payments. Legal constraints: most US-domiciled EMIs apply jurisdiction policies that reject RMI-registered entities, reflecting correspondent-bank de-risking; balances at EMIs are held at the partner licensed bank and must be booked and audited in the RMI BC's financial statements; investor capital and escrow funds should never be held at an EMI and must remain at a tier-1 RMI commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory at the Bank of Marshall Islands: at least one authorized signatory must attend the Majuro branch in person, and all directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners must submit notarized or apostilled identification, proof of address, and source-of-wealth statements. Bank of Guam permits a discretionary remote-opening pathway using video identity verification, apostilled corporate records, and a structured video/telephone interview, but may escalate to face-to-face attendance for high-risk profiles or non-US passport signatories. No fully digital 'remote-first' corporate onboarding exists in the RMI. For the escrow account, the bank will also require a board resolution defining the escrow purpose, the release conditions, and the named signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident Business Corporation with wholly foreign ownership, no physical RMI premises, no local employees, and no demonstrable economic substance (offshore shell red flag).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing issued by the RMI Registrar of Corporations; apostilled board resolutions authorizing the account opening and appointing signatories; a complete corporate organizational chart identifying all shareholders through to natural-person UBOs at the 25% threshold; certified passports and proof of residential address for all directors and UBOs; current negative-media and sanctions screening reports (World-Check/Dow Jones) for all related parties; two years of audited financial statements or, for a start-up, a board-approved business plan with projected transaction volumes and a detailed source-of-funds narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity, nominee shareholder arrangements, or perceived association of the jurisdiction with offshore tax structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory beneficial-ownership register extract; executed UBO declarations including source of wealth and source of funds; share register and share-allotment ledger evidencing issuance and consideration; an irrevocable undertaking to notify the bank of any change in directors, shareholders, or UBOs within 14 days; professional reference letters from the RMI registered agent, outside counsel, and accountants; if the BC is parented, the parent entity's complete KYC pack with financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ISIC 3240 product exposure: interactive AI robotic companion animals with speech synthesizers may be flagged for dual-use or export-control classification, and for sanctions/destination risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: US Commerce Department ECCN classification memorandum (initial expectation: EAR99, non-ITAR, civilian consumer application); product technical white paper and user documentation demonstrating non-military use; end-user and end-use certificates executed by all distributors; a written OFAC and restricted-party screening policy; customer due-diligence files for each sales channel; logistics evidence (commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading) proving genuine physical trade flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pacific island jurisdiction exposure: correspondent-bank de-risking and perceived weaknesses in AML supervision of small USD-based banking systems.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of real economic substance and trade activity: purchase orders, supplier contracts, warehouse inventory records, and shipping documents; audited or reviewed financial statements; adopted AML/CFT compliance policies aligned with the AMLCFTA 2012 and RMI Banking Commission guidance; written commitment to route all clearing exclusively through the bank's correspondent network; periodic external compliance attestations; RMI's Asia/Pacific Group (APG) mutual-evaluation follow-up documents demonstrating supervisory progress.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital moves in USD via SWIFT MT103 over CHIPS/Fedwire to the BMI or Bank of Guam correspondent accounts. The MT103 remittance field 70 must state the economic purpose: 'Equity capital contribution in cash' (classified as Direct Investment — Equity under IMF BPM6) or 'Share subscription proceeds', referencing the board resolution and the company's share allotment register. Shareholder loans must be supported by a signed loan agreement and coded as Direct Investment — Intercompany Debt. The RMI imposes no registration, no approval, and no exchange-control filing for inward investment. Verification discipline: the receiving bank matches the wire against corporate authorizations, applies FATF-consistent customer due diligence, screens against OFAC sanctions lists, and files currency-transaction or suspicious-transaction reports as applicable; any single remittance of USD 100,000 or more should be prefaced with a source-of-funds letter and a short business plan. Escrow-grade investor capital should be held at BMI, operational funds at a second bank to avoid concentration risk, and Stripe/credit-card proceeds swept from the US merchant subsidiary via daily ACH or MT103 as intercompany settlements recorded in the RMI BC's books.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 in USD via Fedwire/CHIPS from the BMI or Bank of Guam account to supplier banks in China, Taiwan, Vietnam, or Mexico, with MT103 fields 70 and 72 carrying the commercial invoice and purchase-order references. Large-value or strategic purchases: commercial documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) issued under UCP600, payable at sight or on 30-90 day usance drafts, advised and, where prudent, confirmed by a major Asian issuing bank. Secondary rails: (i) fintech EMI accounts (Mercury/Evolve, Airwallex) for sub-threshold supplier payments and payroll in USD; (ii) US ACH for domestic vendors of the US subsidiary; (iii) Stripe payout sweeps from the merchant-of-record subsidiary to the treasury account. Outbound USD is unrestricted under RMI law; the only operative limitations are the bank's OFAC screening, suspicious-transaction reporting, and the documentary evidence supporting each trade settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/CNY, USD/TWD, and USD/VND foreign-exchange forwards with tenors up to 12 months, supported by confirmed purchase orders
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNY (onshore) and KRW for currencies lacking onshore deliverability or restricted convertibility
Cross-currency interest rate swaps converting USD floating-rate liabilities into CNY/CNH fixed-rate obligations for term financing
Outright USD call and put options on CNY and TWD for contingent cash-flow hedging
Structural natural hedging through USD-denominated supplier contracts, cross-border netting, and invoice-currency alignment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations (administered by International Registries, Inc.)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through March 31 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of US$500 assessed immediately after March 31; additional penalty of US$1.00 per day of continued non-filing; administrative dissolution or strike-off after 90 days of non-compliance without reinstatement rights.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit for non-resident exempt Business Corporations. An audit is triggered only by shareholder resolution, lender covenant, or parent-company consolidation requirements under IFRS.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or U.S. GAAP as adopted by the board of directors; no local Marshall Islands GAAP exists.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation filing is required. Registered agent and director changes must be filed with the Registrar within 30 days. Annual Report confirms current directors and registered agent; no beneficial owner disclosure is made to the public registry.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; if prepared for financing or transparency, US$2,500 - US$6,000 for a typical small entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% — the Republic of the Marshall Islands imposes no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, and no branch profits tax on the worldwide income of a Non-Resident Business Corporation.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Complete and automatic exemption for non-resident domestic corporations under the Business Corporations Act 1990 (as amended). No tax holiday application, ruling, or incentive filing is required. The only recurring statutory charge is the flat annual report filing fee (minimum USD 50, scaled by authorized share capital tier). The regime also imposes no payroll tax, no VAT/GST, no net worth tax, and no withholding tax on distributions. Any loss carryforward provisions applicable to resident taxpayers are moot for the zero-rated non-resident BC.
